sidebar_encrypted: End-to-end encrypted: the server sees only ciphertext.
detail_not_found: There is no such entry here.
groups_intro: Groups share vaults with several people at once.
welcome_text: Create a new company or open the invitation link you received.
setup_code_hint: It is in the server's settings.
passphrase_hint: At least four words or 16 characters. Nobody can reset it.
kit_text: With the account ID, the Secret Key and your passphrase you unlock a new device; the Recovery Key gets you into your account if you forget the passphrase. Write them down or print them and keep them safe.
kit_saved: I have stored the recovery kit safely.
error_invalid_invitation: This invitation is no longer valid.
error_too_many: Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes.
error_wrong_passphrase: Passphrase or Secret Key is wrong.
error_unreachable: The server cannot be reached, and this device has no copy yet to unlock without it.
error_unexpected: That did not work. Try again.
kit_qr: Scan this code with a new device: it fills in server, account ID and Secret Key. You type the passphrase yourself; the Recovery Key is not in the code.
kit_keep: Keep this sheet safe, in a safe or with your documents. Whoever has it and knows your passphrase can get into your account. Nobody can reset your passphrase or Recovery Key for you.
error_wrong_recovery_key: The account ID or Recovery Key is wrong.
recover_text: The Recovery Key from your Recovery Kit gets you back into your account. Then you choose a new passphrase and get a new Recovery Kit; nobody can sign in with the old Recovery Key after that.
pair_text: Scan this code with the camera of a device where Kennwort is unlocked, or open Settings → Add device there and paste the link below.
pair_code_question: Does the other device show the same code?
pair_waiting: Waiting for the other device to confirm …
pair_failed: Connecting did not work. Start again.
add_text: On the new device, open “Connect with another device” and scan its code with the camera, or paste the link here.
add_code_question: Does the new device show the same code? Only then add it.
add_error_link: This is not a link to connect.
add_error_gone: This connection no longer exists. Start it again on the new device.
add_error_key: The server delivered a different key than the code shows. The device was not added.
devices_load_failed: The devices could not be loaded.
devices_remove_failed: The device could not be signed out.
members_invite_hint: Valid for seven days and only once. Send it by a channel you trust.
members_confirm_mismatch: These keys do not belong to your invitation. Kennwort does not confirm them.
members_confirm_used: You already confirmed this invitation for another account.
members_root_mismatch: The company key from the server does not match your account. Kennwort therefore shows no members.
members_load_failed: The members could not be loaded.
members_confirm_other_keys: Your device knows other keys for this account. Kennwort does not confirm these.
members_role_failed: The role could not be changed.
members_root_grant_invalid: The company key the server gives you is not your company's. Kennwort does not accept it.
members_root_adopt_failed: The company key could not be taken over just now. Try again.
policy_invalid: The policies from the server are not validly signed. Kennwort keeps to the last valid ones.

match.count=one: Kennwort locks after 1 minute without use.
match.count=*: Kennwort locks after {minutes} minutes without use.

policy_saved: Saved. The new time applies on all devices.
policy_failed: The policies could not be saved.
policy_unreachable: The policies could not be loaded. Kennwort keeps to the last valid ones.
vaults_unreachable: The vaults could not be loaded or checked.
vaults_refused: A vault whose log does not add up – it stays closed.
vaults_create_uncertified: You can create a vault once your keys are confirmed.
vaults_create_failed: The vault could not be created.
vaults_untrusted: The vaults cannot be checked: the server's company key does not match your account. If your company has a new one, confirm it under “Members”.
vault_members_stale: Another device just changed the vault. The new state is loaded – please try again.
vault_members_failed: The change could not be saved.
vault_members_until_hint: After this day no device opens the vault for this person.
no_access_intro: You are not a member of this vault. Its managers can add you; Kennwort shows them your request.
no_access_sent: Your request is with the vault's managers.
no_access_failed: The request could not be sent.
vault_members_past: That day is already over. Choose today or a later day.
groups_intro_real: Groups organise the company, for example by team. Whoever joins a group shows up as a request for the managers of its vaults; only a manager grants access.
groups_failed: The groups could not be loaded or changed.
vault_groups_hint: Whoever is in a linked group, or joins it, shows up under “Requests”. Unlinking takes nobody's access.
entry_editor_read_only: You may only read in this vault.
entry_editor_failed: The entry could not be saved. It waits on this device until the server answers again.
totp_invalid: Not a valid key for one-time codes
totp_hint: The key or the otpauth link from the service's setup page
qr_scan_intro: Hold the QR code from the service's setup page up to the camera, or choose a screenshot of it.
qr_not_found: There is no QR code in this image.
qr_not_totp: This QR code holds no key for one-time codes.
qr_no_camera: Kennwort may not use the camera. Choose a screenshot instead.
offline_synced: Last sync: {time}. Changes need the connection again.
offline_never: No sync on this device yet.
update_ready: A new version is ready, checked and signed.
share_intro: Share this entry with someone from the company who is not in the vault. They can only read it, also after later changes. If you remove them, Kennwort encrypts the entry anew.
share_until_hint: After this day no device opens the entry for this person.
share_no_candidates: There is nobody left to share with: every confirmed person of the company is in the vault or has the entry already.
share_failed: That did not work. Try again.
share_not_renewed: The entry could not be encrypted anew; the share is still in place. Try again once you are connected.
share_not_current: Someone changed the entry at the same moment. The share is removed and the entry encrypted anew; please share it with the others again.
detail_favorite_failed: The favorite was not saved. Try again.
detail_weak: The password is weak and easy to guess.
detail_reused: The same password is used in {count} entries.
popup_connect_text: Your recovery kit shows the server, the account ID and the Secret Key. The extension remembers them until you close the browser.
popup_no_page: No website is open in this tab.
popup_load_failed: The entries could not be loaded. Lock and unlock again.
popup_untrusted: The server delivered a different company key than the known one, so Kennwort shows nothing.
error_invalid_server: That is not a valid server address.
error_insecure_server: The server must be reachable over HTTPS.
error_invalid_account: The account ID or Secret Key is not in the right format.
error_storage_failed: The extension could not store the keys protected. Restart the browser.
error_server_unreachable: The server cannot be reached. Check the address and the connection.
vault_members_uncertified: A member has no confirmed keys. Without them Kennwort cannot change the vault key, so nobody was removed.
vault_members_rewrite_failed: The vault key has changed, but not every entry is encrypted again yet. Kennwort tries again the next time it opens.
rotation_due: The vault {name} is waiting for a key change: someone was removed, and a manager still has to encrypt the vault again. Until then nobody can change anything in it.
entry_editor_rotation_due: This vault is waiting for a key change. Until a manager makes it, nobody can change anything in it.
members_leave_text: {name} can no longer reach the server, starting now. Kennwort takes them out of the vaults you manage, changes their keys and puts what they could read under “To change”.
members_leave_failed: This person could not be removed from the company.
report_intro: What this person could read, as far as your vaults show it. Change these passwords; the entries are also listed under “To change”.
report_none: This person was not a member of any of your vaults.
inline_menu_foreign: Kennwort fills nothing into this frame: it belongs to another website than the page.
inline_menu_hidden: The menu was covered or transparent. Kennwort filled nothing in.
inline_menu_not_filled: Kennwort filled nothing in: the page no longer matches the entry.
inline_menu_unverified: This browser cannot confirm that the menu is visible. Copy the user name and password from the popup.
inline_menu_keys: ↑↓ choose · Enter fill in · Esc close
import_intro: Bring your logins from another password manager or browser. Kennwort reads the export file on this device only; only the encrypted entries go to the server.
import_vendor_step: Where are your logins coming from?
import_howto_title: How to get the export file
import_howto_bitwarden_json: In Bitwarden's web vault open “Tools” → “Export vault”, choose the format “.json”, or “.json (Encrypted)” with the export type “Password protected”, and confirm with your master password. Kennwort opens a password-protected export with its export password.
import_howto_bitwarden_csv: In Bitwarden's web vault open “Tools” → “Export vault”, choose the format “.csv” and confirm with your master password. Cards and identities only come along with the JSON export.
import_howto_lastpass_csv: In LastPass's web vault choose “Advanced options” → “Export” and confirm with your master password; LastPass downloads a CSV file.
import_howto_onepassword_csv: In the 1Password 8 desktop app choose “File” → “Export”, pick the account, take “CSV” as the format and confirm with your account password.
import_howto_onepassword_1pux: In the 1Password 8 desktop app choose “File” → “Export”, pick the account, take “1PUX” as the format and confirm with your account password. Choose the .1pux file as it is; attachments stay out.
import_howto_keepass_kdbx: Choose the database file (.kdbx) as KeePass 2, KeePassXC or Passbolt’s “KDBX” export saves it, and open it with its master password; if the database has a key file, choose it as well. Kennwort reads KDBX 4 – save an older database as KDBX 4 in KeePassXC or KeePass first.
import_howto_keepass_xml: Open the database in KeePass or KeePassXC, choose “File” → “Export” and take “KeePass XML (2.x)” or “XML file”.
import_howto_keepassxc_csv: Open the database in KeePassXC and choose “Database” → “Export” → “To CSV file”.
import_howto_keepass_csv: Open the database in KeePass 2, choose “File” → “Export” and take “KeePass CSV (1.x)”.
import_howto_passbolt_csv: In Passbolt select the passwords, choose “Export” and take “CSV (KeePass)” as the format.
import_howto_dashlane_csv: In Dashlane's web app download the CSV export under “Settings” → “Export data” and unzip it; import each CSV file in it on its own.
import_howto_dashlane_zip: In Dashlane's web app download the CSV export under “Settings” → “Export data” and choose the ZIP as it is, without unzipping it.
import_howto_protonpass_json: In Proton Pass under “Settings” → “Export” choose “JSON” without PGP encryption, unzip the file and take “data.json”.
import_howto_protonpass_zip: In Proton Pass under “Settings” → “Export” choose “JSON” without PGP encryption and choose the downloaded ZIP as it is.
import_howto_keeper_csv: In Keeper's web vault choose “Settings” → “Export”, take “CSV” and confirm with your master password.
import_howto_nordpass_csv: In the NordPass app choose “Settings” → “Export items” and confirm with your master password; NordPass saves a CSV file.
import_howto_enpass_json: In the Enpass desktop app choose “File” → “Export”, pick the vault, take “.json” as the format and confirm with your master password.
import_howto_tpm_csv: In Team Password Manager, as an admin or IT user, choose “Passwords” → “Export” (or “Export” in a project) and download the CSV file. Each project becomes a folder.
import_howto_cxf_json: In the other password manager, save the export in the “Credential Exchange Format” (CXF) as an unencrypted JSON file. Passkeys come along when their key is ES256.
import_howto_chrome_csv: In Chrome or Edge open “Settings” → “Passwords” (Google Password Manager), then “Settings” → “Export passwords” and confirm. Brave and Opera export the same way.
import_howto_firefox_csv: In Firefox open “about:logins”, choose “Export logins” in the “…” menu and confirm with your device password.
import_howto_safari_csv: On the Mac open the Passwords app (or Safari → “Settings” → “Passwords”) and choose “File” → “Export All Passwords”.
import_howto_google_authenticator: In Google Authenticator on your phone, choose “Transfer accounts” → “Export accounts” and pick the accounts. The app shows one or more QR codes; scan each of them here.
import_howto_aegis_json: In Aegis, choose “Settings” → “Import & Export” → “Export”, take the format “Aegis (.JSON)” and turn off “Encrypt the vault”.
import_howto_twofas: In 2FAS, choose “Settings” → “2FAS Backup” → “Export to file” and export without a password; 2FAS saves a .2fas file.
import_howto_table: Save the spreadsheet as CSV with commas between the columns and a header row that names every column. Then you map the columns.
import_howto_other: Export your logins from the app into an unencrypted file and choose it here.
import_file_hint: The file stays on this device and is not uploaded.
import_qr_intro: Hold Google Authenticator's export QR code up to the camera, or choose a screenshot of it.
import_qr_not_migration: This QR code is not a Google Authenticator export.
import_qr_paste: Or paste export links (otpauth-migration://…), one per line
import_qr_hint: The QR codes stay on this device and are not uploaded.
import_qr_empty: Scan a QR code or paste an export link first.
import_qr_wrong: This is not a Google Authenticator export link.
import_kdbx_key_file: Key file (only if the database has one)
import_kdbx_opening: Decrypting the database – this can take up to a minute …
import_kdbx_hint: Database, password and key file stay on this device; Kennwort does not store the password.
import_error_not_text: This file is not text. Choose the export file itself; for a KeePass database take “KDBX”, for a ZIP the vendor with “ZIP” or “1PUX”.
import_error_bad_csv: The CSV file is damaged: a quote is never closed.
import_error_bad_json: This is not a valid JSON file. Did you choose the right format?
import_error_bad_xml: This is not a valid XML file, or it has a document type Kennwort does not read.
import_error_wrong_format: This file does not match the chosen vendor. Check the vendor or take “Other spreadsheet”.
import_error_encrypted: This file is encrypted – export it unencrypted.
import_error_bad_zip: This is not a readable ZIP file, or it is damaged. Download the export again and choose it without unzipping it.
import_error_unsupported_zip: This ZIP is packed in a form Kennwort does not read. Take the export as the vendor delivers it, not repacked.
import_error_too_large: This file is larger than any export, or packed unusually tightly. Kennwort does not read it.
import_error_incomplete: QR codes of this export are missing. Scan every QR code Google Authenticator shows.
import_error_wrong_key: The password or key file does not match this database.
import_error_bad_kdbx: This database is damaged or incomplete. Take a fresh copy of the .kdbx file.
import_error_unsupported: This database has an older format (KDBX 3.1 or older) or an encryption Kennwort does not read (Twofish). Save it as KDBX 4 with AES-256 or ChaCha20 in KeePassXC or KeePass, or export it as XML.
import_error_too_costly: Decrypting this database takes more than Kennwort allows (Argon2 with at most 1 GiB of memory, 100 passes and 256 lanes, AES-KDF with at most 100 million rounds). Lower the values in the database settings or export it as XML.
import_error_bad_key_file: The key file is damaged: its version or checksum does not match.
import_error_unreadable: The file could not be opened.
import_map_intro: Tell Kennwort which column holds what. Columns without a mapping are left out.
import_code_target: Where does the one-time code of {title} go?
import_code_own: Create a login of its own
import_code_conflict_text: “{title}” ({username}) already has another one-time code. Kennwort does not overwrite it; this code gets a login of its own.

match.n=one: 1 code goes into an existing login.
1 entry exists already and is skipped.
match.n=*: {count} entries exist already and are skipped.

match.n=one: 1 weak password – you'll find it under “To change” afterwards.
match.n=*: {count} weak passwords – you'll find them under “To change” afterwards.

match.n=one: Kennwort does not take 1 code because it is no time-based one-time code (TOTP), such as HOTP or Steam. Set it up again with the service.
match.n=*: Kennwort does not take {count} codes because they are no time-based one-time codes (TOTP), such as HOTP or Steam. Set them up again with the services.

match.n=one: Kennwort does not take 1 passkey because its key is not ES256 or the file does not hold all of it. Sign in there with the password and create a new passkey.
match.n=*: Kennwort does not take {count} passkeys because their key is not ES256 or the file does not hold all of them. Sign in there with the password and create new passkeys.

import_offline: Offline – importing works again once the server answers.
import_no_vault: There is no vault you may write in right now.
import_stopped_rotation: The import stopped: a key change is due in the vault. Until a manager makes it, nobody can change anything there.
import_stopped_read_only: The import stopped: you may only read in this vault.
import_stopped_failed: The import stopped: the server did not answer. If you import the file again, entries already saved are marked as duplicates.
import_delete_file: Delete the export file now, from Downloads and the trash too: it holds every password in plain text.
import_to_change: See the weak passwords under “To change”
save_prompt_updated: Updated. The old password is under “Earlier passwords”.
save_prompt_hidden: The bar was covered or transparent. Kennwort saved nothing.
save_prompt_read_only: You may only read this entry, so Kennwort cannot save the new password.
save_prompt_rotation_due: A key change is due in this vault. Until a manager makes it, nobody can change anything there.
save_prompt_no_vault: There is no vault you may save to.
save_prompt_unverified: This browser cannot confirm that the bar is visible. Save the login in the web app.
alert_text: You typed the password of “{title}”. It belongs to {site}, but this page is {host}. Only enter it on {site}.
alert_hidden: The warning was covered or transparent. Click again once you can see all of it.
recovery_on: Company recovery is on: an owner can restore your access if you lose your passphrase and recovery kit.
recovery_off: Company recovery is off: whoever loses passphrase and recovery kit loses the account.
recovery_other_key: The server serves a recovery key the policy does not name. Your access was not deposited.
recovery_unreachable: The state of the deposit could not be loaded.
recovery_new_key_hint: Make a new one when an owner has left: everyone then deposits anew.
recovery_saved: Saved. All devices follow the new policy.
recovery_failed: Company recovery could not be changed.
recovery_start: Lost everything? Recover through your company
recovery_device_text: Show this code to an owner of your company. They scan it with their unlocked device, or paste the link below under Settings → Add device, and choose you.
recovery_device_passphrase: Your account is back. Choose a new passphrase; you get a new recovery kit.
recovery_device_failed: Recovering did not work. Start it again.
recovery_device_untrusted: The account the server delivers is not confirmed by your company's root key. It was not opened.
add_recovery_code_question: Does the device show the same code? Only then restore the access.
add_recovery_done: Access is restored. The device now sets a new passphrase.
add_error_no_key: You hold no valid company recovery key.
add_error_no_deposit: No access is deposited for this member.
add_error_refused: The deposit fails the check. Access was not restored.
emergency_intro: If something happens to you, a person you trust can reach your entries after a waiting time. Until it ends you can object to any request. Your device encrypts the keys for exactly this person; the server cannot open them.
emergency_view_hint: The person can read the chosen vaults and change nothing. After a key change your device renews the access the next time it opens.
emergency_full_hint: The person gets your account's key and can read all your vaults, your personal one too.
emergency_none_given: You have not given anyone emergency access yet.
emergency_none_received: Nobody has given you emergency access.
emergency_failed: That did not work. Please try again.
emergency_load_failed: Emergency access could not be loaded or checked.
emergency_waiting: The waiting time is still running.
emergency_refused: Kennwort refused the release: it does not match what was requested and signed.
emergency_vault_refused: This vault fails the check and stays closed.
emergency_request_notice: {name} asks for emergency access. Without an objection it opens on {date}.
passkey_prompt_hidden: The bar was covered or transparent. Kennwort signed nothing.
passkey_prompt_unverified: This browser cannot confirm that the bar is visible. Use another device.
passkey_prompt_excluded: Kennwort already holds a passkey for this account.
passkey_prompt_none: Kennwort holds no matching passkey for this website.
passkey_prompt_no_vault: There is no vault you may save into.
passkey_prompt_failed: That did not work. Try again or use another device.
renew_intro: If your recovery kit got into someone else's hands, renew every key of your account. Afterwards the old kit and the old keys open nothing written from then on.
renew_step_keys: You get a new Account Key, a new Secret Key, new keys and a new recovery kit. Your passphrase stays.
renew_step_confirm: An owner or admin confirms your new keys with a comparison code. Until then you can read but not change anything.
renew_step_vaults: Then every vault you are in gets a new key.
renew_step_devices: Your other devices are signed out; you pair them again.
renew_step_shares: Shares and emergency access you gave no longer count afterwards; you give them again.
renew_passphrase_hint: To be safe, enter your passphrase once more.
renew_code_title: Comparison code of your new keys
renew_code_text: Show this code to an owner or admin, ideally in person or on the phone. They compare it under Members and confirm your new keys.
renew_conflict: Another device just changed something. Try again.
renew_refused: The server did not take the new keys.
renew_damaged: What the server delivers does not match your account. Nothing was changed.
renew_unreachable: The server cannot be reached. Nothing was changed.
members_renewed_text: {name} renewed their keys. Compare this code with the one {name} sees on their own device, ideally in person or on the phone. Confirm only if every digit matches.
members_renewed_failed: The new keys could not be confirmed.
rotation_due_renewed: Someone in the vault {name} has new keys because a recovery kit got into other hands. Until they are confirmed and the vault has a new key, nobody can change anything in it.
export_intro: Take one vault, or every vault this device opens, out of Kennwort: as an encrypted file for Kennwort, as a KeePass database or as a spreadsheet for other password managers. The file is made on this device only.
export_not_allowed: Only owners and admins of the company may export. Ask them if you need an export.
export_format_json_hint: For Kennwort, with everything: fields, history, tags, favorites, one-time codes and passkeys. Protected by a passphrase.
export_format_kdbx_hint: For KeePass, KeePassXC and anything that reads KDBX. Protected by a password; favorites and passkeys stay out.
export_format_csv_hint: For other password managers. Not protected: every value is in the file in plain text.

match.n=one: At least 1 character. Without it the file cannot be opened – not even by Kennwort.
match.n=*: At least {count} characters. Without it the file cannot be opened – not even by Kennwort.

match.n=one: The passphrase needs at least 1 character.
match.n=*: The passphrase needs at least {count} characters.

export_passphrase_mismatch: The two passphrases do not match.
export_csv_warning: Warning: the CSV file is not encrypted. Anyone who opens it sees every password, one-time code and note. Load it into the other password manager right away and delete it afterwards, from Downloads and the trash too. Do not open it in a spreadsheet.
export_csv_confirm: I understand that the file is not encrypted.
export_csv_confirm_missing: First confirm that you want an unencrypted file.
export_audit_hint: Every export goes into the audit log with your name, the scope and the format before the file is made.
export_busy: Recording the export in the audit log and making the file – this can take a few seconds …
export_error_empty: There is no vault this device can open in this scope.
export_error_refused: The server did not record the export in the audit log. Without an entry there is no export – check the connection and try again.
export_done_keep: Keep the file and its passphrase apart and safe.
export_done_csv: Delete the CSV file as soon as the other password manager has read it – from Downloads and the trash too.
import_howto_kennwort_json: Choose the file Kennwort wrote as encrypted JSON under “Settings” → “Export”, and enter its passphrase.
import_kennwort_hint: File and passphrase stay on this device; Kennwort does not store the passphrase.
import_error_kennwort_wrong_key: The passphrase does not match this export.
import_error_kennwort_unsupported: This export comes from a newer version of Kennwort. Update Kennwort and try again.
import_bitwarden_hint: This export is password protected. Enter the password you set when exporting from Bitwarden – not your master password. File and password stay on this device.
import_error_wrong_password: The password does not match this file. Check it and try again.
import_error_damaged: The file is damaged or was changed. Export it again and choose the fresh file.
import_error_account_encrypted: This Bitwarden export is “account restricted”: it is encrypted with your Bitwarden account and only opens there. Export again as “.json (Encrypted)” with the export type “Password protected”, or as “.json”.
import_error_bitwarden_unsupported: Kennwort does not read this export: it names a key derivation or encryption that Bitwarden does not write this way. Export it again in Bitwarden.
import_error_cxf_unsupported: This file has a newer version of the Credential Exchange Format than Kennwort reads (version 1). Export in version 1 from the other manager if you can.
import_error_bitwarden_too_costly: Decrypting this export takes more than Kennwort allows (PBKDF2 with at most 2 million iterations, Argon2id with at most 1 GiB of memory, 10 passes and 16 threads).
export_error_failed: The file could not be written. The export is already in the audit log; try again.
members_root_fork: The server shows two changes of the company key from the same old key. This is an attack: Kennwort takes neither and shows no members.
members_root_retired: The server serves a company key your company has replaced. Kennwort no longer takes it and shows no members.
root_code: Comparison code of the company key
root_code_text: Every member checks a new company key with this code before taking it.
root_replace_text: Whoever left as an owner or admin still has the old company key. Kennwort creates a new one and confirms every member anew with it. Each member takes it only after comparing the new code with you.
root_replaced: The new company key is in force. Compare this code with every member:
root_replace_failed: The company key could not be replaced.
root_change_text: Your company has a new company key. Compare this code with an owner, best in person or on the phone. Take it only if every digit matches.
root_change_failed: The new company key could not be taken.
secret_intro: Someone sent you something confidential with Kennwort. The link opens only a limited number of times: show the content only when you need it.
secret_gone: This link has expired, was revoked or has been opened as often as allowed. Ask for a new one.
secret_damaged: The content does not match this link. It was changed on the way, or the link is incomplete.
secret_broken: This link is incomplete. Copy all of it from the message again.
secret_passphrase_intro: This link is also protected by a passphrase. You got it another way, by phone for example.
secret_used_up: The link is now used up. Copy what you need: once you close the page, the content is gone.

match.n=one: The link can be opened 1 more time.
match.n=*: The link can be opened {count} more times.

secret_footer: Kennwort decrypted the content on your device only. The server does not know it.
link_intro: A link for someone without an account. It expires and opens only as often as you choose. Anyone with the whole link can read the content.
link_nothing: This entry has no fields that can go into a one-time link.
link_passphrase_hint: Pass it on another way, by phone for example. Without it the link opens nothing.
link_made_note: The link is valid until {date}. Kennwort shows it only now: copy it and send it on.
link_too_large: Too much for a one-time link. Shorten the text or share fewer fields.
link_failed: The link could not be created. Try again.
links_intro: Send a secret to someone without an account, a craftsman or the tax adviser for example. Kennwort encrypts it on your device; the key is only in the link.
links_failed: The links could not be loaded or revoked.
notifications_load_failed: The notifications could not be loaded.
notifications_hint: The server announces notifications. Kennwort checks what they name where you open it.
notifications_invitation_accepted: {name} accepted your invitation. Compare the code and confirm the person.
notifications_member_renewed: {name} has new keys. Compare the code and confirm them.
notifications_root_changed: {name} changed the company key. Confirm the change.
notifications_emergency_requested: {name} asks for emergency access. Object if you do not want that.
notifications_emergency_answered: {name} answered your request for emergency access.
notifications_account_recovered: {name} recovered your account on a new device.
notifications_link_opened: One of your one-time links was opened.
notifications_security_report: Your monthly security report is ready.
push_settings_text: A push notification says only “New notification in Kennwort”. The app fetches what happened only when you open it.
push_on: Push notifications are on for this device.
push_unsupported: This browser or server offers no push notifications.
push_denied: The browser does not allow Kennwort to notify. You can change that in the browser's settings.
push_failed: Push notifications could not be turned on.
push_kinds_failed: The choice could not be saved.
security_intro: What to do about the passwords in your vaults. Worked out on this device; no password leaves it.
security_leak_toggle: Check passwords against known data breaches
security_leak_explain: Of each password only the start of its SHA-1 hash (5 characters) goes through your Kennwort server to Have I Been Pwned; the comparison happens on this device. Applies to your account only.
security_leak_off: Off. No request goes out until you switch it on.
security_leak_unavailable: Your Kennwort server does not offer the check.
security_leak_limited: Too many requests. Try again in a few minutes.
security_leak_failed: The check did not work just now. Try again later.
security_leak_save_failed: The setting could not be saved. Are you online?
security_report_intro: For owners and admins: how the passwords in the vaults you can open are doing. Counts only, no titles.
security_report_save_failed: Could not be saved. Are you online?
oidc_enrol_text: You signed in with the identity provider. Now choose your passphrase: with it and your Secret Key you unlock Kennwort. The identity provider never sees either.
oidc_error_state: The sign-in expired or belongs to another window. Please try again.
oidc_error_provider: The identity provider does not answer. Please try again later.
oidc_error_token: The identity provider's answer could not be verified.
oidc_error_left: This account is no longer part of the company.
oidc_error_no_company: No company can be joined through the identity provider right now. Ask your admin for the link to join.
oidc_error_linked_elsewhere: This sign-in already belongs to another account.
oidc_error_already_linked: Your account is already linked to another sign-in.
oidc_error_ticket: This sign-in has been used already. Please sign in again.
oidc_waiting_text: Your account has been created but not confirmed yet. An owner or admin compares your code with you, ideally in person or on the phone, and confirms you. Only then can vaults be shared with you.
oidc_waiting_company: The company's code: it must match the one your admin reads to you.
members_enrolled_text: {name} signed in with the identity provider. The identity provider only confirms who signs in, not the keys. Compare this code with the one {name} sees, in person or on the phone. Confirm only if every digit matches.
members_enrolled_company: Then read the company's code to {name}:
members_enrolled_failed: The account could not be confirmed.
oidc_link_text: Your groups then follow the identity provider. You keep unlocking with your passphrase.
oidc_link_failed: The identity provider cannot be reached right now.
oidc_enrolment_text: Whoever signs in through the link gets an account without vaults. You confirm it only after comparing a code.
oidc_enrolment_failed: The setting could not be saved.
oidc_groups_text: A group follows the identity provider's group of the same name. Joining is only an access request; access comes from a manager of the vault.
notifications_member_enrolled: {name} signed in with the identity provider and waits for the code check.
notifications_group_left: {name} is no longer in the identity provider's group for {vault}. Remove {name} there if the access should end.
push_kind_member_enrolled: New sign-in via the identity provider
push_kind_group_left: Left a group at the identity provider
label_intro: For the device or installation this entry belongs to. The QR code leads to the entry in Kennwort.
label_no_secret: The code holds only the entry's address, no password. Only someone who unlocks Kennwort and may read the entry can open it.
label_unavailable: No label can be printed for this entry.
companies_intro: One account, several companies: each company has its own keys, vaults and members. Your account opens them for you, without another passphrase.
companies_manage_at_home: You can add and remove companies in your own company.
companies_name_hint: What the company is called in your account; only you see the name.
companies_name_taken: Please give the company a name.
companies_link_broken: That is not a complete invitation link.
companies_join_hint: An owner or admin of the company sent you the link.
companies_setup_hint: The setup code is set by whoever runs the server.
handover_intro: The vault goes end-to-end encrypted to another company of your account, such as your customer's.
handover_stays: The vault here stays as it is. Kennwort now switches to the chosen company.

match.n=one: 1 entry goes into a new vault of this company.
match.n=*: {count} entries go into a new vault of this company.

handover_no_customer: Nobody in this company is confirmed yet who could take the vault over.
handover_keep: Afterwards you stay in the vault with “Edit”, e.g. for maintenance, but no longer manage its members.
handover_customer_decides: Then the customer decides: they can remove you entirely at any time, and the vault gets a new key.
handover_failed_create: The vault could not be created. Are you confirmed in this company yet?
handover_failed_entries: Not all entries could be written. The new vault is incomplete.
handover_failed_customer: The customer could not be added. The new vault is still yours.
handover_failed_role: Your access could not be reduced. Change your role under the vault's “Members”.
cli_help_login: login              Connect this computer to your account: server, account ID, Secret Key, passphrase
cli_help_unlock: unlock             Check the passphrase and the server; nothing stays unlocked afterwards
cli_help_lock: lock               Nothing to do: Kennwort keeps no key between two commands
cli_help_search: search <query>     Search entries by title, username and address
cli_help_get: get <entry>        Print a field of an entry (ID or whole title), only after confirmation
cli_help_logout: logout             Disconnect this computer from the account
cli_help_account: --account <ID>     Account ID from the recovery kit (login)
cli_help_field: --field <field>    Which field (get): password, username, website, totp …; without: the password
cli_help_stdin: --passphrase-stdin Read the passphrase from the first line of stdin instead of the terminal
cli_help_exit: Exit codes: 0 done, 1 error, 2 wrong usage, 3 not confirmed, 4 not found
cli_unlocked: Passphrase and server checked. Vaults: {vaults}, entries: {entries}. Nothing stays unlocked.
cli_locked: Nothing unlocked: Kennwort keeps no key between two commands.
cli_logged_out: This computer has forgotten the account.
cli_refused_vaults: Warning: {count} vaults not opened, their log fails the check.
cli_refused_entries: Warning: {count} entries refused, they fail the check.
cli_error_missing_argument: {value} needs an argument. Help with kennwort --help
cli_error_not_logged_in: This computer knows no account. First: kennwort login
cli_error_no_terminal: No terminal to type into. The passphrase works with --passphrase-stdin, the confirmation with --yes.
cli_error_invalid_server: That is not the address of a server.
cli_error_insecure_server: Only over HTTPS; http works only for localhost.
cli_error_invalid_account: The account ID or the Secret Key does not have the form of the recovery kit.
cli_error_wrong_passphrase: The passphrase, account ID or Secret Key is wrong.
cli_error_too_many_requests: Too many attempts. Try again later.
cli_error_untrusted: The server's data fails the check. Nothing opened.
cli_error_damaged_device_file: {path} is damaged. Connect anew with kennwort login
cli_error_not_found: No entry with this ID or title: {value}. Search with kennwort search
cli_error_ambiguous: Several entries are called “{value}”. Use the ID:
cli_error_no_field: The entry has no such field: {value}. Fields: {fields}
cli_error_invalid_totp: The one-time code key cannot be read.
notifications_update_available: A newer version of Kennwort is out. Ask whoever runs your server to update it (kennwort.app/updates.html).
privacy_stored_intro: The server stores only what it needs to answer requests. It cannot read anything that is encrypted.
privacy_stored_account: Your account: a random ID, your company, your role and when it was created
privacy_stored_keys: Your public keys and your certificate; your private keys and your account state only encrypted
privacy_stored_vaults: Vaults and entries only encrypted, along with the signed membership logs
privacy_stored_devices: Your devices and sessions (name, browser, IP address, times), passkeys and push addresses
privacy_stored_notifications: Notifications to you, with IDs, never with names
privacy_stored_audit: The company's audit log: who did what when, with account IDs
privacy_never_passphrase: Your passphrase, your Secret Key and your Recovery Key
privacy_never_content: Passwords, notes and everything else in your entries
privacy_never_names: The names of vaults, entries and companies
privacy_data_intro: Download what the server stores about your account as a JSON file (Art. 15 and 20 GDPR).
privacy_entries_export: Your entries themselves are in the app's encrypted export:
privacy_entries_admins: Owners and admins of the company export your entries themselves under Settings → Export.
privacy_delete_intro: Deletes your account on the server: devices, sessions, push addresses, notifications and your encrypted keys. Vaults only you are in are deleted with it; a manager takes you out of shared vaults and the key is changed. Your public keys stay so others can check what you signed.
privacy_delete_at_home: You can delete your account only in your own company.
privacy_delete_warning: This cannot be undone. Confirm with your passphrase.
privacy_delete_linked: These companies are deleted with it:
privacy_error_locked: Too many attempts. Try again later.
privacy_error_last_owner: You are the last owner. Make someone else an owner first.
privacy_error_sole_manager: You are the only manager of a shared vault. Make someone else a manager first.
privacy_error_linked: A linked company cannot be reached right now. Nothing was deleted.
privacy_error_failed: That did not work. Try again.
demo_notice: Runs only in your browser, without a server. Don't enter real passwords; a reload starts over.
demo_preparing: Setting up the demo company Weber Haustechnik …
demo_failed: The demo could not start. Reload the page.
mobile_server_text: Enter the address of your company's Kennwort server; it is in your recovery kit. From then on the app talks to this server only.
mobile_server_storage_failed: The app could not save the address. Restart it and try again.
